idiom_name: EF Core entity-hierarchy mapping (TPH discriminator / ToTable TPT / UseTpcMappingStrategy)
implementation_notes: EF Core owns the mapper hierarchy: the CLR hierarchy is mapped as a whole and the strategy decides its shape - table-per-hierarchy by default with an implicit discriminator column (configured by HasDiscriminator().HasValue<T>()), table-per-type by calling ToTable/UseTptMappingStrategy per type, and table-per-concrete-type via UseTpcMappingStrategy() (EF Core 7+). Materialising a row returns the right CLR type because the discriminator is part of the model, so the generated mapper replaces the classic per-class mapper hierarchy; hand-written mappers remain justified when the SQL itself must be tuned, which is exactly Dapper's role.
pitfalls: TPH makes every subclass column nullable in the shared table, so NOT NULL constraints on subclass properties cannot be enforced there.
TPT joins every table in the inheritance path for each query and is measurably slower than TPH; composite foreign keys/indexes over inherited plus declared properties cannot be created.
A discriminator value present in the database but absent from the model throws when EF materialises the row; either map every value or mark the discriminator IsComplete(false).

variants.name: Hand-written Dapper row mappers per class
variants.implementation_notes: Dapper deliberately maps single result sets to single objects, so inheritance is the developer's problem: one mapper or query per class, a discriminator switch or a separate query per table for the class-table shape, and explicit joins when a subclass needs the base columns. This is the classic mapper-hierarchy work done on top of a micro-ORM - choose it when query shape and SQL cost matter more than having the ORM resolve polymorphism for you.
pitfalls: dynamic rows defeat compile-time checking: a renamed column fails at runtime, so hand-written mappers need tests (or Query<T> with explicit column lists).
The discriminator fall-through silently returns base-class objects for unknown type codes; handle the default case explicitly.
Each mapper function duplicates the base column list unless the base projection is factored out into a shared SELECT fragment.
